I would change Ryan’s code from **SC to UA**, because he has said he was not ill, and his sister does not meet the stated definition for DEP. BRV does not apply, and the absence was not booked in advance.

Before noon, I would also:

- Add a factual note that Ryan called Gary before his shift, that his sister went into labour unexpectedly, and that he took her to hospital and stayed with her. I would not suggest he failed to notify his team leader.
- Urgently email payroll and any available senior HR or operations manager, explaining that the UA will be his second during probation and will trigger a termination letter at 12:00. I would ask whether they can pause the letter and arrange an urgent human review, including whether an exception or statutory protection applies. I would copy the HR Manager, but not rely on a reply today.

If no authorised intervention is confirmed before payroll runs, I would leave the accurate UA code in place and make clear in my escalation that the letter is expected to be issued. Keeping SC would knowingly give payroll a false reason for the absence; the note alone will not prevent the probation consequence.

Ryan’s circumstances and prompt call make this a case for urgent review, even though they do not fit another code under the rules given.
